question: Should OpenClaw adopt `sessions.diagnose` as a supported public Gateway and CLI diagnostic contract, including its stable finding-code vocabulary and native-client protocol models?
rationale: The implementation is additive and evidence-backed, but choosing a permanent operator API and its compatibility commitments is a product and ownership decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded diagnosis contract
options.body: Accept the read-only RPC and CLI as the supported operator diagnosis surface, then require a clean rebase and final exact-head review before merge.

options.title: Narrow the public result first
options.body: Ask the contributor to reduce or revise the finding/result vocabulary before accepting a smaller durable public contract.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep the existing session tools and close or redirect the feature only if maintainers do not want a core diagnostic API.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded diagnosis contract
recommendation.body: Accept the read-only RPC and CLI as the supported operator diagnosis surface, then require a clean rebase and final exact-head review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent gateway-diagnostics history makes this the best available routing candidate in the supplied evidence, though explicit sessions/Gateway ownership is not established here.
